falsifier: A checked-in positive fixture or retail function whose exact relocation/dataflow provenance satisfies every stated condition yet the recovered per-bctr target map differs from the linker-resolved control flow, or an adversarial fixture in tools/gdl/tests/test_webfrank.py that the implementation accepts despite ambiguous, malformed, overlapping, incomplete, cross-function, or target/current-disagreeing provenance.
subject: tool:webfrank
value: A WebFrank CFG proof for a function containing multiple bctr sites must not give every site the union of every address-taken target in the function. Each bctr is soundly refined only when its own immediate lwzx -> mtctr -> bctr chain traces exactly one load base through an unbroken same-basic-block ADDR16_LO/ADDR16_HA pair naming one defined, aligned, non-empty table; every word in that table must carry exactly one R_PPC_ADDR32 relocation resolving inside the current function. Missing, ambiguous, duplicate, overlapping, incomplete, wrong-type, cross-function, or target/current-disagreeing provenance must refuse. Measured on DoPlayerAction: the old union connected the first dispatch to blocks reachable only from two later switches, bypassed a real +0x1320 definition, and produced a false value-equality refusal; per-dispatch maps for the three sites removed only those impossible edges, after which the verifier exposed three genuine source semantic errors and finally proved the 1765/1765 closure.
